01 / Built for the review before the merge

From a risky change
to a clearer decision.

A review comment is a starting point. AegisPR is built to connect it to a repeatable experiment and an inspectable result.

Open interactive test build ↗

No API keys, GPU, Docker or paid calls.
Not a live PR review or model-generated test.

  1. 01

    Open the experiment

    Start with a cart total of 10 and a discount of 20. Choose the buggy change.

  2. 02

    Run the boundary check

    The base clamps the total to zero; the changed version returns −10. The same assertion passes on base and fails on the change.

  3. 03

    Inspect the manual repair

    Try the prewritten repair, then change the inputs and run again. A passing example only verifies that input and assertion.

Full local setup and troubleshooting ↗
  1. 01

    Start the isolated judging build

    The command launches the real UI and API on loopback ports 3300 / 18080, then executes fixed Python and Node tests in Docker.

  2. 02

    Unlock a printed report URL

    In “Private deployment access”, enter the local code from artifacts/judge/access-code. Never publish that code or use a provider key here.

  3. 03

    Read the execution receipts

    Expand base, changed and manual-repair results. Inspect commands, logs and exit codes. Tests and repairs are prewritten; this build uses no model inference or GPU ranking.

Full pipeline · setup required

From a public PR
to tested evidence.

Requires a configured private deployment, usable Nebius credits, Docker and the NVIDIA driver / Container Toolkit for GPU ranking.

Live inference and an actual PR acceptance run are not yet verified for this deployment. The public website does not run this pipeline.

Read the deployment guide ↗
  1. 01

    Configure secrets on the server

    Copy .env.example to .env, configure the Nebius key and separate worker / app access secrets. Keep all provider keys off the website.

  2. 02

    Start and authenticate

    Run docker compose up --build -d. Open localhost:3000 and enter the private app access code. Use HTTPS for any internet-accessible deployment.

  3. 03

    Verify, inspect, then re-prove

    Paste a public GitHub PR URL and select “Verify PR”. Inspect the evidence; optionally verify a repair for a confirmed regression. Keep the $20 total / $0.25 per-run / five-attempt admission limits.

05 / A few things worth knowing

Clear answers.
No black box.

Read the documentation ↗
Does the public demo use my tokens?

No. It runs a fixed JavaScript experiment in your browser. The local judging build also uses no model tokens. Only the configured live pipeline calls the inference provider.

Does a passing result mean my PR is safe?

No. A result applies only to the executed checks. Passing tests do not prove general correctness or security. Review the assertion, coverage, environment and skipped checks before deciding to merge.

Will AegisPR edit my GitHub repository?

The verification and repair workflow uses isolated checkouts. A repair proposal is tested there; it does not automatically push changes or merge your PR.

Can I run it without an NVIDIA GPU?

The token-free local judging build needs no GPU. The live pipeline can record a CPU fallback for context ranking; that must not be presented as CUDA execution. Large-model inference is served separately by Nebius.

Can I expose the local judging build publicly?

Do not expose its Docker-socket-backed API as an arbitrary-code service. It is a trusted-operator build with loopback ports and a private access code. Read the security documentation before changing deployment boundaries.
